TCO & CHARGING

Electric Truck TCO Calculator: Energy, Charging, Maintenance and Utilization

A transparent worksheet method for comparing trucks with your own route, tariff, utilization and finance data.

TCO GUIDESeptember 23, 20269 min read
In this guideScopeFormulaEnergyInfrastructureInputs

Core rule: use the same duty cycle, ownership period, currency, tax treatment, financing basis and annual work for every vehicle. A TCO model is useful only when its assumptions are visible and replaceable.

Define the comparison first

Choose the exact task: cargo or trailer, payload, loaded and empty distance, grade, speed, shifts, operating days and depot return pattern. Set analysis years and annual kilometres. Compare vehicles able to complete the same work. A cheaper chassis is not a valid alternative if it cannot carry the body, payload or combination mass.

Separate one-time investment, recurring cost and end value. State whether inputs include tax, duty, finance and inflation. Convert quotations to one currency and date. Do not compare a cash purchase with financed payments without calculating financing cost.

Use a complete TCO formula

Total costAcquisition + financing + charging infrastructure + energy + maintenance + tyres + insurance + taxes + downtime - verified incentives - residual value
Cost per productive kilometreTotal cost / productive kilometres completed during the period

Productive kilometres must reflect availability. If charging, maintenance or route mismatch prevents dispatch, include the lost work. Fleets managed by tonnes, pallets or trips should also calculate cost per tonne-kilometre, pallet or completed cycle.

Calculate energy from the route

Use measured consumption for loaded, partial and empty legs. Multiply each distance by its kWh per kilometre, then add cab climate control, refrigeration, tipping, mixing or other auxiliaries. Include charging losses using metered grid energy when available. Battery capacity is not consumption and cannot alone determine range or cost.

Annual electricity costGrid energy by tariff period x electricity price, plus demand charges and site energy fees

Model peak and off-peak energy separately. If demand charges apply, estimate coincident charger demand under the dispatch plan. Test low, base and high cases for consumption, tariff and annual work. For operational detail, see the charging planning guide.

Allocate charging assets fairly

Include chargers, transformer or grid upgrade, switchgear, cabling, civil works, permits, software, commissioning and maintenance. Do not charge the whole depot to the first truck when it is designed for a larger fleet. Show initial cash flow and allocate shared assets across expected vehicles and service years.

Model redundancy. A low-cost installation with no spare connector can create expensive downtime. Include service fees, inspections and the operational space required for charging bays.

Maintenance, tyres and battery assumptions

Use written schedules and local parts and labour rates. Separate planned maintenance from repair contingency. Include tyres for the actual axle layout, load and surface. Do not assume a universal maintenance saving: body equipment, brakes, cooling and high-voltage components still require service.

Do not invent battery replacement timing, degradation or residual value. Use final warranty and operating documents. Where future values are uncertain, show scenarios rather than hiding uncertainty in one estimate.

Utilization can dominate the result

Higher productive use spreads vehicle and infrastructure cost over more work, but reduces charging time and raises the value of reliable dispatch. Model charger queues, loading, driver shifts and maintenance. Check whether one vehicle can cover two shifts or charging requires additional fleet capacity.

Worksheet inputs

  • Delivered vehicle and body price, taxes, duty and finance.
  • Analysis years, annual work and utilization.
  • Loaded, partial and empty consumption.
  • Tariffs, demand charges and charging losses.
  • Charger, grid, civil, software and service costs.
  • Maintenance, tyres, insurance and registration.
  • Downtime and backup-vehicle assumptions.
  • Verified incentives, warranty and residual scenarios.

Frequently asked questions

Should purchase price decide?

No. Energy, utilization, infrastructure, maintenance, finance and residual value can change lifecycle cost.

Can a range claim be used?

Use route-specific consumption. Payload, speed, grade, temperature and auxiliaries affect energy.

How are shared chargers treated?

Show initial cash investment and allocate the asset over its expected fleet and service period.
